ai.description: This gecko reaches 60–70 mm. It features a dark brown body with distinct white transverse bands and a white-spotted head. It is distinguished by a slender, cylindrical tail and Gekkonidae classification.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus albofasciatus* is uniquely identified by the distinct, continuous white vertebral stripe running down its back, which is absent in other Indian *Hemidactylus*.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus albofasciatus* inhabits the rocky outcrops and lateritic plateaus of the northern Western Ghats, typically found in dry deciduous scrub forests at low altitudes.
ai.behavior: The White-striped Viper Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to actively forage for small insects among rocky outcrops and vegetation.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus albofasciatus* is oviparous, laying a single hard-shelled egg per clutch. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus albofasciatus* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, typically inhabiting rocky outcrops at low to moderate elevations.
